issuer: the West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles
note: The West Virginia Code on code.wvlegislature.gov (read 2026-10-30): § 17B-2-8 charges $5 for each year a Class E licence is valid and § 17B-2-12 makes a licence expire eight years from issue, so an eight-year licence costs $40 (the sum is held); § 17B-2-3a issues the level three full Class E licence from 17 (level two before). § 17B-2-1 issues an identification card from age 2 for $5 a year, expiring on a birthday at an age divisible by five and issued for no less than three years and no more than seven; a five-year card, $25, is held. Not held: the $10 more for a federally compliant (REAL ID) licence or card, a licence or card under 21 expiring 30 days after the 21st birthday.

sources.title: W. Va. Code § 17B-2-8, Fees for licenses
sources.said: The fee for the issuance of a Class E driver’s license is $5 per year for each year the license is valid.

sources.title: W. Va. Code § 17B-2-12, Expiration of licenses
sources.said: every driver's license expires eight years from the date of its issuance.

sources.title: W. Va. Code § 17B-2-3a, Graduated driver’s license
sources.said: may be issued a level three full Class E license without further examination or road skills testing if the licensee: (1) Has reached the age of 17 years;

sources.title: W. Va. Code § 17B-2-1, Identification cards
sources.said: Has reached the age of two years ... Has paid the required fee of $5 per year. ... no identification card may be issued for less than three years or for more than seven years and expires on the licensee’s birthday in those years in which the licensee’s age is evenly divisible by five.
